options: A standalone record holding reusable client-side JavaScript, not tied to any single form, Client Script, or UI Page
A special type of UI Page that renders without any HTML
A one-time script that runs only during instance upgrades
A server-side Script Include that can only be called from Business Rules
questions.explain: A UI Script is pure reusable client-side JavaScript, callable from any Client Script, UI Policy, or UI Page that includes it.

questions.q: What does checking the Global box on a UI Script do?
options: The script loads automatically on every page in the instance, rather than only where explicitly included
It converts the UI Script into a server-side Script Include
It deletes the script from every table that referenced it
It restricts the script to a single form only
questions.explain: Global makes the UI Script load on every page automatically; unchecked, it loads only where explicitly included by name.

options: A JavaScript error is thrown
The literal text 'null'
An empty string, because the guard clause returns '' before any Date object is created
The current date
questions.explain: The `if (!dateString)` guard returns an empty string immediately, avoiding creating a Date from an empty value.

questions.q: A validation function now appears, copy-pasted, in two separate Client Scripts on different tables. What does this lesson say to do?
options: Convert both Client Scripts into Business Rules instead
Extract the function into a UI Script and have both Client Scripts include it, so there's one place to fix a bug instead of two
Leave both copies as-is since Client Scripts can never share logic
Delete one of the two copies and accept that only one table gets the validation
questions.explain: A second copy of the same client-side function is the signal to extract it into a shared UI Script, mirroring the Script Include discipline from Chapter 3.

questions.q: What is the real parallel between a UI Script and a Script Include from Chapter 3?
options: UI Scripts run on the server and Script Includes run in the browser
There is no meaningful parallel between the two
Both exist for reusability — Script Includes share server-side logic, UI Scripts share client-side logic — even though the mechanics (classes, GlideAjax) differ
They are the exact same record type, just renamed for different ServiceNow versions
questions.explain: Both solve the same reusability problem on their respective side of the application — one place to fix or extend a shared function.
